columns.pickEach: Pick the column that holds each part. Under it is what the first of its {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} has there.
columns.pickTitle: Pick the column that holds the title
columns.untitledLeftOut: {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} without a title left out

upload.notSent: The file couldn't be sent. Try again.
upload.uploadedPdfs: {count, plural, one {# uploaded PDF} other {# uploaded PDFs}}

why.notReadable: Not a kind of file a screening reads
why.tooBig: Over {mb, number} MB: split it and add each part
why.noTable: No table of references in it

upload.drop: Drop reference files or PDFs here
upload.fileLimit: Reference files up to {mb, number} MB
upload.pdfLimit: PDFs up to {mb, number} MB each
upload.aboutFiles: A reference file is what a database or a reference manager exports. Each of its records with a title and an abstract is a paper.
upload.aboutPdfs: A PDF is read as soon as it is added, for its title and its DOI. Where Openscholar's index holds that DOI, the paper shows with the index's title and abstract. Otherwise the paper is the PDF: a person screening it reads the file, and so does each AI reviewer, every page of it. A scan is read the same way. A file that doesn't open is left out.
upload.kinds: RIS, BibTeX, EndNote, PubMed, Web of Science, CSV and PDF, any number at once
upload.pdfCost: A model reads each PDF's first pages for its title and DOI: up to {credits} credits a PDF, paid as it is added

pdf.fileWithPages: Read as its PDF, {count, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}}

dois.notAdded: The DOIs couldn't be added. Try again.
dois.label: DOIs
dois.forms: Bare, as doi.org addresses, or inside a reference list
dois.takenOnce: A DOI pasted twice is taken once
dois.about: Openscholar looks each DOI up in its index, then in Crossref and DataCite, and takes the paper's title and abstract from there. The ones none of them has a record of, and the ones whose record has no abstract, are left out and listed on the source's row once it has been read.
dois.placeholder: Paste DOIs, or any text that holds them
dois.twice: {count, plural, one {This DOI is already a source} other {These DOIs are already a source}}
dois.none: No DOI in what you pasted

zotero.connectWhy: Connect it to pick from your library and the groups you are in.
zotero.aboutUnder: About {count, number} with what is under it
zotero.subTakenOnce: A paper filed in two of them is taken once
zotero.subAbout: Zotero counts only the items filed directly in a collection, and so does the count here. With this on, a collection is added with the papers of every collection under it: what they hold together is about what Zotero counts in each, added up, and exact once the screening has read them.
zotero.readingCount: Reading its collections, {read, number} of {total, number}
zotero.failed: Zotero couldn't be read. Open the library again.
zotero.itemsInZotero: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} in Zotero
zotero.noneFound: No collection of {library} has {text} in its name.
